rows.speaker: رواية
rows.claim: An alternate report identifies Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam and his daughters as the sorcerers; Gabriel disclosed the well and spell, which ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, and ʿAmmār retrieved, and recitation of both refuge-suras undid its eleven knots and cured the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ان الذى تولى السحر لبيد بن الاعصم وبناته فمرض النبى صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فنزل جبريل بالمعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī judges the first narration, whose preceding details fall outside this excerpt, more sound than the sorcery account just given.
rows.anchor: والرواية الأولى أصح من هذه

rows.speaker: المازري
rows.claim: Al-Māzarī says innovators reject the sorcery report because it compromises prophethood and could undermine confidence in revealed law.
rows.anchor: قد أنكر ذلك الحديث المبتدعة من حيث انه منصب النبوة ويشكك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that the report is sound and neither opposes revelation nor diminishes prophethood; the disbelievers' bewitched meant mad, and any effect concerned ordinary human affairs rather than the prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: الحديث صحيح وهو غير مراغم للنص ولايلزم عليه حط منصب النبوة والتشكيك فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that God protects the Prophet in matters of conveying revelation; the charge may refer to madness, an earlier incident, or a false claim that revelation itself was sorcery.
rows.anchor: لأن الكفار أرادوا بقولهم مسحور انه مجنون وحاشاه ولو سلم أرادة ظاهره

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ reads ʿĀʾisha's reports as sorcery affecting the Prophet's body and outward faculties, not his reason, heart, or beliefs.
rows.anchor: ان السحر تسلط على جسده الشريف صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وظواهر جوارحه لاعلى عقله عليه الصلاة والسلام وقلبه واعتقاده

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: On the report that he thought he approached his wives, Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ explains that familiar vigor appeared to him, but the sorcery overcame him when he approached and no intercourse occurred.
rows.anchor: انه يظهر له من نشاطه ومتقدم عادته القدرة عليهن فاذا دنا منهن أخذته أخذة السحر فلم يأتهن

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ treats reports of imagined acts as sensory illusion without a defect in reason, so they create no confusion about the message or opening for hostile criticism.
rows.anchor: فمحمول على التخيل بالصبر لالخلل تطرق إلى العقل وليس فى ذلك ما يدخل لبسا على الرسالة

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ is presented as denying sorcery has real effects and as attributing its apparent effects to baseless imaginings.
rows.anchor: أنكر ونفى السحر حقيقته وأضاف مايقع منه إلى خيالات باطلة لاحقائق لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī sides with Sunni scholars that sorcery has a real nature, since Qurʾān and Sunna indicate its reality.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أهل السنة وعلماء الامة على ثباته وانه له حقيقة كحقيقة غيره من الاشياء لدلالة الكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that reason allows God to disrupt ordinary patterns through crafted words, substances, and combinations of forces; poisons and medicines show that hidden powers can kill or sicken, and sorcery can also act psychologically.
rows.anchor: لايستنكر فى العقل ان الله تعالى يخرق العادة عند النطق بكلام ملفق أو تركيب أجسام مخصوصة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view limits sorcery's effect to separating spouses, arguing that the verse would have named greater effects if they occurred, since comparison at its strongest supports emphasis.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم لايزيد تأثيره على قدرة التفرقة بين المرء وزوجه لان الله تعالى انما ذكر ذلك تعظيما

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī endorses the Ashʿarī view that sorcery can have greater effects: God alone causes them as customary events, and no decisive revelation restricts them to marital separation.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الاشاعرة انه يجوز أن يقع به أكثر من ذلك وهو الصحيح عقلا لانه لا فاعل الا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between a sorcerer's extraordinary effect and a prophet's or saint's miracle is explained in theology books and commentaries on the sound collections.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الساحر وبن النبى والولى على قول الاشاعرة بأنه يجوز خرق العادة على يد الساحر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reads the blowers into knots as people undoing men's resolve through stratagem, likening it to loosening a knot with breath; Al-Ālūsī calls this close to dubious novel exegesis.
rows.anchor: وقيل فى الآية الملراد بالنفث فى العقد ابطال عزائم الرجال بالحيل مستعار من تليين العقد بنفث الريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envier's harm begins when he manifests envy and acts on it through words or deeds that set evil and injury in motion, including an angry envious gaze that may harm the target according to their relative strength.
rows.anchor: اذا أظهر ما فى نفسه من الحسد وعمل بمقتضاه بترتيب مقدمات الشر ومبادى الاضرار بالمحسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envious gaze may inflict harm, even death, much as the gaze of certain snakes is said to harm its target.
rows.anchor: ربما تؤثر فى المحسود بحسب ضعفه وقوة نفس الحاسد شرا قد يصل إلى حد الاهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envier and the evil-eye caster both direct a malign state of soul toward a target, but the evil eye arises at direct sight while envy can operate in absence or presence.
rows.anchor: العائن والحاسد يشتركان فى أن كلا منهما تتكيف نفسه وتتوجه نحو من تريد اذاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An evil-eye caster may affect an animal or crop that he does not envy, though envy is never wholly absent toward its own object.
rows.anchor: العائن قد يعين من لايحسده من حيوان وزرع وان كان لاينفك من حسده صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to envy when acted upon is explained by saying that otherwise it causes no harm; another view says envy harms only the envier.
rows.anchor: والتقييد بذلك اذ لاضرر بل قيل ان ضرر الحسد انما يحيق بالحاسد لاغير

rows.speaker: على
rows.claim: ʿAlī's maxim says envy is strikingly just because it begins by destroying the envier himself.
rows.anchor: لله در الحسد مأعدله بدأ بصاحبه فقتله

rows.speaker: ابن المعتز
rows.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz says to endure an envier, since the fire of envy consumes itself when it finds nothing else to eat.
rows.anchor: اصبر على حسد الحسود فان صبرك قاتله فالنار تأكل بعضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy can mean wishing another's blessing removed, or wishing someone to remain without a blessing; the first sense is more common, and both forms are blameworthy.
rows.anchor: أن الحسد يطلق على تمنى زوال نعمة الغير وعلى تمنى استصحاب عدم النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate envy is not sinful when a person resists acting on it, treats the other as God loves, and struggles against his own disposition; that self-discipline is greatly rewarded.
rows.anchor: الحسد الغريزى الجبلى اذا لم يعمل بمقتضاه من الاذى مطلقا بل عامل متصف به أخاه بما يحب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy is also used figuratively for ghibṭa: wishing to share another's blessing without wishing it removed, which is permissible.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الحسد على الغبطة مجازا وكان ذلك شائعا فى العرف الأول وهى تمنى أن يكون له مثل مالأخيه من النعمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound prophetic report permits ghibṭa only toward two people: one given wealth and spending it rightly, and one given wisdom who judges by it and teaches it.
rows.anchor: ماصح من قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لاحسد الا فى اثنتين رجل آتاه الله تعالى مالا

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: Abū Tammām's poetic line uses envy for the response to a person's deserved glory.
rows.anchor: هم حسدوه لاملومين مجده

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā allegorizes the darkening one as the animal faculty: a murky darkness unlike the rational soul, which is originally pure and receptive to forms and truths.
rows.anchor: الغاسق القوة الحيوانية فهى ظلمة غاسقة منكدرة على خلاف النفس الناطقة

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā reads the blowers into knots as the vegetative faculties, which increase bodily dimensions in length, breadth, and depth as if blowing into three knots.
rows.anchor: والنفاثات فى العقد اشارة إلى القوى النباتية من حيث انها تزيد في المقدار من جميع جهاته الطول والعرض والعمق

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Because the soul relates to vegetative faculties through the animal faculty, Ibn Sīnā says the animal faculty is named first; the bodily ties then block the soul's proper nourishment in knowledge of the enduring realm.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت العلاقة بين النفس الانسانبة والقوى النباتية بواسطة الحيوانية لاجرم قدم ذكر القوى الحيوانية على القوة النباتية

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: In this reading the body, through its two faculties, is the envier and the soul is envied; the soul is better when detached from the body unless it has been contaminated by it.
rows.anchor: فالحاسد هو البدن من حيث له القوتان والمحسود هو النفس فالبدن وبال عليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another allegory assigns the darkening one to minerals, the blowers to plants, and the envier to animals, since human harm comes from elemental bodies rather than celestial ones.
rows.anchor: وقيل الغاسق اشارة إلى المعدن والنفاثات إلى النباتات والحاسد إلى الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two closing chapters are called al-Muʿawwidhatayn, with the waw vowel kasra rather than fatḥa, and also al-Muqashqishatayn.
rows.anchor: وتسمى ماقبلها كما أشرنا اليه قبل بالمعوذتين بكسر الواو والفتح خطأ وكذا بالمقشقشتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Nās has six verses, not seven, despite the choice of some scholars to count seven.
rows.anchor: وهى ست آيات لاسبع وان أختار بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two chapters are recited with the hamza of qul aʿūdhu omitted and its vowel transferred to the lām, like the cited reading of fa-khudh arbaʿata.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فى السورتين بحذف الهمزة ونقل حركتها إلى اللام كما قرىء فخذ أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lord of people means the owner of their affairs and their nurturer, granting what benefits them and warding off what harms them.
rows.anchor: مالك امورهم ومربيهم بافاضة مايصلحهم ودفع ما يضرهم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والدورى عن الكسائى
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and al-Dūrī from al-Kisāʾī use imāla for al-nās here and wherever the word occurs in the genitive.
rows.anchor: وأمال الناس هنا أبو عمرو والدورى عن الكسائى وكذا فى كل موضع وقع فيه مجرورا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Following al-Zamakhsharī, al-Ālūsī parses King of people as an appositional clarification: divine nurture is complete ownership and sovereign disposal, unlike ordinary masters' care of slaves.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان على ماأختاره الزمخشرى جىء به لبيان ان تربيته تعالى اياهم ليست بطريق تربية سائر الملاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being God of people clarifies that His sovereignty is more than political rule, management, and protection: it is worship grounded in divinity and complete power over life, death, creation, and annihilation.
rows.anchor: بل هو بطريق المعبودية المؤسسة على الالوهية المقتضية للقدرة التامة على التصرف الكلى فيهم احياء واماتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Substitution is also a rationally possible grammatical parsing for the titles, though the appositional clarification was chosen, perhaps for its eloquence.
rows.anchor: وجوزت البدلية أيضا وأنت تعلم أنه لامانع منه عقلا ثم ماهنا وان لم يكن جامدا فهو فى حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilāh al-nās distinguishes Gods divinity from kings, whose utmost role is political rule, managing affairs, and protecting their subjects.
rows.anchor: ليس بمجرد الاستيلاء عليهم والقيام بتدبير أمور سياستهم والتولى لترتيب مبادىء حفظهم وحمايته كما هو قصارى أمر الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although all creation is under God's lordship, dominion, and divinity, mentioning people guides them to genuine refuge: the seeker belongs to the very class of nurtured, owned servants, drawing special mercy.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الاضافة إلى الناس مع انتظام جميع العالم في سلك ربويته تعالى وملكوته والوهيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to seek refuge carries a gracious promise of protection; naming people as His servants and subjects signals their rescue from Satan's rule, as affirmed in scripture.
rows.anchor: وأمره تعالى بذلك من دلائل الوعد الكريم بالاعاذة لامحالة ولان المستعاذ منه شر الشيطان المعروف بعداوتهم

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: One scholar explains the focus on people as fitting because refuge here concerns whispering that targets human souls; al-Ālūsī objects that the whisperer's harm also reaches bodies.
rows.anchor: اقتصر بعض الاجلة فى بيان وجه التخصيص على كون الاستعاذة هنا من شر مايخص النفوس البشرية وهى الوسسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the explanation that people are specified because whispering targets human souls incomplete, since the whisperer's evil can also affect bodies.
rows.anchor: بأن شر الموسوس كما يلحق النفوس يلحق الابدان أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the title Lord of people recalls their primordial covenant to acknowledge God's lordship, urging refuge from whispering that could stain it; this too hints at promised protection.
rows.anchor: تذكير الأول أمر عرفوه فى عالم الذر وأخذ عليهم العهد بالاقرار به فيما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that Ibn Sīnā's discussion here is so troubling to those familiar with sacred law that pens shrink from recording it.
rows.anchor: ولابن سينا ههنا كلام تتحرج منه الاقلام كما لايخفى على من ألم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating people provides further clarification and emphasis and honors them through the possessive relation to God.
rows.anchor: وتكرير المضاف اليه لمزيد الكشف والتقرير والتشريف بالاضافة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative avoids repetition by assigning the first people to fetuses and children needing nurture, the second to youths needing governance, and the third to elders devoted to worship; al-Ālūsī finds this unlikely because the repeated definite noun normally signals identity.
rows.anchor: فالناس الأول بمعنى الاجنة والاطفال المحتاجين للتربية والثانى الكهول والشبان لانهم المحتاجون لمن يسوسهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes waswās as a verbal noun meaning whispering; its kasra form first denotes the sound of jewelry or a faint murmur, then an evil thought, and here Satan is named after his act, or understood as possessor of whispers.
rows.anchor: الوسواس عند الزمخشرى اسم مصدر بمعنى الوسوسة والمصدر بالكسر وهو صوت الحلى والهمس الخفى

rows.speaker: بعض أئمة العربية
rows.claim: Some Arab grammarians distinguish true quadriliteral faʿlala verbs from reduplicated forms and give both regular verbal nouns faʿlala and faʿlāl; the kasra is more regular, while fatḥ is common with reduplication, and the pattern can express intensity.
rows.anchor: ان فعلل ضربان صحيح كدحرج وثنائى مكرر كصلصل ولهما مصدران مطردان فعللة وفعلال بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says waswās is an adjective, so the verse needs neither figurative usage nor an elided possessor; he points back to the same discussion in Sūrat al-Zalzala.
rows.anchor: والحق أنه صفة فليحمل عليه ما فى الآية الكريمة من غير حاجة إلى التجوز أو حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense seeks refuge from the evil of the whisperer as such, which ultimately means the evil of his whispering; a broader reported reading seeks protection from all his evils and makes bodily harm more plausible.
rows.anchor: والظاهر ان المراد الاستعاذة من شر الوسواس من حيث هو وسواس ومآله إلى الاستعاذة من شر وسوسته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī says the whisperer ties three knots at a sleeper's crown to keep him from waking; al-Ālūsī says its bodily harm is unclear.
rows.anchor: كما فى صحيح البخارى يعقد على قافية رأس العيد اذا نام ثلاث عقد مراده بذلك منعه من اليقظة

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Some count demonic seizure or confusion among the whisperer's harms, which Sunnis allow can occur through demonic touch, as discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم عد من التخبط اذا لحق عند أهل السنة انه قد يكون من مسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannās is an intensive form or a relational adjective for one whose habit is to withdraw when a person remembers God.
rows.anchor: صيغة مبالغة أونسبة أى الذى عادته أن يخنس ويتأخر اذا ذكر الانسان ربه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍiyāʾ, al-Ḥākim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and others transmit from Ibn ʿAbbās that every newborn has whispering on the heart; it retreats when the child matures and remembers God and whispers when heedless. Al-Ḥākim authenticates the report.
rows.anchor: أخرج الضياء فى المختارة والحاكم وصححه وابن منذر وغيرهم عن ابن عباس قال مامن مولود يولد الا على قلبه الوسواس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report attributed to Qatāda describes the whisperer as having a snout like a dog's.
rows.anchor: وله على ماروى قتادة خرطوم كخرطوم الكلب

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Ibn Shāhīn transmits from Anas that he heard the Prophet describe the whisperer as bird-beaked: when a person is heedless it whispers into the heart's ear, and when God is remembered it recoils, explaining its name.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن شاهين عن أنس قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقول أن للوسواس خطما كخطم الطائر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take people’s breasts figuratively to mean their hearts.
rows.anchor: قيل أريد قلوبهم مجازا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Satan enters the chest, like an anteroom to the heart, to deliver suggestions; reason permits this, and revelation—including the report that Satan moves through a person like blood—requires accepting it.
rows.anchor: ان الشيطان يدخل الصدر الذى هو بمنزلة الدهليز فليقى مايريد ألقاءه إلى القلب

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Others take the language figuratively and argue that the verse itself does not require physical entry into a person.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من حمله على التمثيل وقال فى الآية انها لاتقتضى الدخول

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā identifies the whisperer with imagination when the animal soul employs it: unlike the rational soul, which faces separate principles, imagination draws toward material attachments and then recedes.
rows.anchor: الوسواس القوة التى توقع الوسوسة وهى القوة المتخيلة بحسب صيرورتها مستعملة للنفس الحيوانية

rows.speaker: ابن سينا
rows.claim: Another account makes it the estimative faculty, which assists reason through premises, then withdraws at the conclusion and begins to whisper doubts; al-Ālūsī says it should not be treated as exegesis of God's speech and assumes the Qāḍī offered it only as analogy.
rows.anchor: ماقيل انه القوة الوهمية فهى تساعد العقل فى المقدمات فاذا آل الامر اللى النتيجة خنست وأخذت توسوسه وتشككه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun can be genitive as an adjective, or nominative or accusative as an expression of censure; in the latter parses, readers may pause at khannās.
rows.anchor: ومحل الوصول اما الجر على الوصف واما الرفع والنصب على الذم والشتم

rows.speaker: الكواشي والطيبي والكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kawāshī disallows pausing at khannās when it is adjectival; al-Ṭībī questions this because of the end rhyme, while al-Kashf accepts a good pause only as a special rhyme-ending case.
rows.anchor: ففى الكواشى أنه لايجوز الوقف وتعقبه الطيبى بان فى عدم الجواز نظر للفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can explain that whisperers are of two kinds, jinn and humans, as in the Qurʾānic pairing of human and jinn devils.
rows.anchor: بيان للذى يوسوس على أنه ضربان جنى وأنسى كما قال تعالى شياطين الآنس والجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the prepositional phrase attaches to whispering and marks its source: jinn suggest that beings benefit or harm, while astrologers and soothsayers among humans claim knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: ومن لابتداء الغاية أى يوسوس فى صدورهم من جهة الجن مثل أن يلقى فى قلب المرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammatical possibilities make the phrase circumstantial from the subject of whispering, a substitution for from evil with an elided noun, or a partitive substitution for whisperer.
rows.anchor: وجوز فيه الحالية من ضمير يوسوس والبدلية من قوله تعالى من شر باعادة الجار وتقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others take people as including jinn, citing al-Kalbī's expression people among the jinn and the labels company and men; al-Ālūsī says common usage and the rhetorical relation of whole to part make this unlikely.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء وجماعة انه بيان للناس بناء على أيه يطلق على الجن أيضا فيقال كما نقل عن الكلبى ناس من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preceding interpretation one would have to say the devil whispers in human breasts, but there is no proof for that and the verse cannot be used to establish it.
rows.anchor: بانه يلزم عليه القول بان الشيطان يوسوس فى صدور الانس ولم يقم دليل عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A closer proposal reads people as the forgetful, with the yāʾ omitted as in the cited readings; jinn and humans then clarify who forgets.
rows.anchor: أن يراد بالناس الناسى بالياء مثله فى قراءة بعضهم من حيث أفاض الناس بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading each member of both groups forgets God's due unless protected by divine preservation and mercy.
rows.anchor: فان كل فرد من أفراد الفريقين مبتلى بنسيان حق الله تعالى الا من تداركه شوافع عصمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One symbolic count says the chapter has twenty-two distinct letters, like al-Fātiḥa, matching the years of revelation; al-Ālūsī notes the count should be checked and the common view gives twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: أن حروف هذه السورة غير المكرر اثنان وعشرون حرفا وكذا حروف الفاتحة وذالك بعدد السنين التى أنزل فيها القرآن

rows.speaker: بعض الفرس
rows.claim: Another symbol reads the first and final letters, bāʾ and sīn, as بس, meaning enough, and takes them to suggest that the Qurʾān contains everything.
rows.anchor: أن أول حروفه الباء وآخرها السين فكأنه قيل بس أى حسب

rows.speaker: بعض الفرس
rows.claim: The cited Persian couplet glosses the opening and closing letters as saying that in both worlds the Qurʾān is enough, one among many symbolic readings.
rows.anchor: يعنى اندرد وجهان رهبر ما قرآن بس ومثله من الرموز كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī cautions against saying that the chapter simply intends to teach seeking divine aid as in al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: لاينبغى أن يقال أن مراد الله عز وجل فلى هذه السورة إلى الاستعانة به تعالى شأنه كما أرشد جل وعلا اليها فى الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If surah order was divinely revealed, ending the Book with refuge from whispering can signal the high rank of taqwā, the core of the matter and the route to a good ending.
rows.anchor: بل لايبعد أن يكون مراده تعالى على القول بان ترتيب السور يوحيه سبحانه من ختم كتابه الكريم بالاستعاذة به تعالى من شر الوسواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his closing prayer al-Ālūsī asks for protection from Satan and his snares and for his descendants to become learned and righteous guides.
rows.anchor: وأعذنى من وساوس الشيطان ومكايده ومن الارتباك بشباك غروره ومصايده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī records completing the commentary on Tuesday night, the fourth of Rabīʿ al-Thānī 1267 AH.
rows.anchor: ليلة الثلاثاء لاربع خلون من شهر ربيع الآخر سنة ألف ومائتين وسبع وستين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is tested through blessing; God honors him with wealth and expands his provision, so he concludes that God has honored him by what He gave.
rows.anchor: امتحنه ،   { ربه } بالنعمة ،   { فأكرمه } بالمال ،   { ونعمه } بما وسع عليه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir read qaddara with a doubled dāl; the other readers use the lighter form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر { فقدر } بتشديد الدال ،   وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forms are dialect variants and mean that God constricted the person's provision; another explanation takes qadara as qattara, giving only what suffices.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان ،   أي ضيق عليه رزقه .   وقيل : قدر بمعنى قتر وأعطاه قدر ما يكفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the disbeliever, who measures honor and humiliation by abundance or scarcity of wealth and worldly fortune.
rows.anchor: وهذا يعني به الكافر ،   تكون الكرامة والهوان عنده بكثرة المال والحظ في الدنيا وقلته

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say the verse was revealed about the disbeliever Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل : نزلت في أمية بن خلف الجمحي الكافر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the verse is not about one named individual, but about the class of disbelievers who equate honor and disgrace with worldly wealth and fortune.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ليس المراد به واحدا بعينه ،   بل المراد جنس الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's pain reaches the hearts; the word for rising or appearing can mean reaching, as in the Arab expression asking when one's land was reached.
rows.anchor: أي التي يبلغ ألمها ووجعها إلى القلوب ،   والاطلاع والبلوغ بمعنىً واحد ،   يحكى عن العرب : متى طلعت أرضنا

rows.speaker: القرظي والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Quraẓī and al-Kalbī say the fire consumes everything until it reaches a person's heart.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية : أنها تأكل كل شيء منه حتى تنتهي إلى فؤاده ،   قاله القرظي والكلبي
